subject: SLA contingency request — automated degrade and sticky-version for EU checkout peak
messages:
From: Mikael Lindström <ops@nordicpay.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: EU checkout spike — request for SLA contingency

Hi Lauren and team,

We're expecting a coordinated marketing push on Friday (2026-05-22) that will triple checkout traffic across EU gateways for a ~6 hour window. Our SREs are concerned about persistent tail latency for the Redwood-powered verification step under burst QPS.

What we need: an authorized contingency plan that permits automatic runtime degradations if p95 or p99 latency crosses configured SLOs, specifically:
- Allow routing to a smaller, quantized variant for up to 20% of EU checkout traffic as a protective hedge.
- Permit a \"sticky version\" (sticky-routing/pinning) for sessions that start on the fallback variant to avoid cross-variant cache thrash.
- Automatic revert to primary model once telemetry shows sustained recovery.

We'd like a formal exception/approval by EOD Thu (2026-05-21) with clear responsible contacts and failover criteria. I'm attaching our traffic forecast and a telemetry snapshot.

Thanks,
Mikael
Ops Lead, NordicPay
[Attachment: contingency_policy_v2.pdf]
[Attachment: telemetry_snapshot_2026-05-20.png]

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Mikael Lindström <ops@nordicpay.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 11:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: EU checkout spike — request for SLA contingency

Mikael — thanks for the heads up and for the attachments.

High level: we can support the pattern you describe, but it requires an SLA carve-out/exception for the EU checkout route for the duration of the event. Concretely we propose the following mitigation bundle:

1) Pre-approved automatic degrade policy
   - If p99 latency > 1200ms for > 3 consecutive minutes, route up to 20% of new checkout requests to \"redwood-tiny-q4\" (4-bit quantized variant) in eu-west region.

2) Sticky-session pinning
   - Sessions routed to the quantized variant will be pinned for 30 minutes (sticky TTL) to preserve KV cache locality and prevent oscillation.

3) Telemetry gating and auto-revert
   - Continuous watch on p95/p99 + error-rate. Auto-revert when p99 < 800ms for 10 consecutive minutes.

4) Rollout safety net
   - We will enable canary telemetry on 5% traffic for the first 30 minutes when policy is turned on, then scale to 20% if signals are stable.

Approval ask: need explicit sign-off from Redwood leadership to authorize the SLA exception for the time window and the sticky-pin policy. Also confirm that NordicPay ops is OK with the 30-minute sticky TTL.

I'll loop in Marcus for the telemetry gating knobs and Marissa for the rollout ops checklist.

- Lauren
Director, Account Solutions — Redwood Inference

Lauren — quick notes from infra/serving runtime:

- The suggested \"redwood-tiny-q4\" variant exists and has consistent perf characteristics at p95 for short sequences. It is already in the model catalog with a validated quantization profile.
- Sticky pinning for 30 minutes is implementable via routing cookie + KV-tag; we'll include jitter to avoid synchronized expirations.
- Telemetry gating: we'll wire an immediate alert that triggers an autoswitch rollback if error-rate increases by >0.5 percentage points after switching.
- Operational cost: the tiny variant increases per-token latency slightly but reduces tail amplification; estimated cost delta for the event ~+6% on token spend for affected traffic.

Actionables for approval:
- Leadership sign-off on temporary SLA carve-out window: Fri 2026-05-22 09:00 — Fri 2026-05-22 15:00 UTC (with option to extend by 2 hours).
- Confirmed fallback policy parameters (p99 thresholds, sticky TTL, max routed percent).

I'll prepare a short runbook and an ops checklist for the event.

Marissa
Sr. Product Ops, Redwood Inference

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com

Subject: Re: SLA contingency request — automated degrade and sticky-version for EU checkout peak

Thanks all — tagging leadership approval thread.

Approval request (for records):
- Approve temporary SLA exception for NordicPay EU checkout route for Friday 2026-05-22, 09:00–15:00 UTC (extendable by ops).
- Approve automatic degrade to redwood-tiny-q4 for up to 20% of traffic when p99 > 1200ms for 3+ minutes.
- Approve sticky-version (pin) TTL 30 minutes for sessions routed to the tiny variant.
- Approve telemetry gating: auto-revert after p99 < 800ms for 10 consecutive minutes; abort switch and rollback if error-rate increases >0.5pp.

If approved, Marissa will publish the runbook and I will send a signed exception notice to NordicPay.

Please reply in-line with APPROVE / REJECT / REQUEST CHANGE.

- Lauren
